title: Amazon's Prime number was a long-kept secret
summary: Amazon began reporting its Prime membership numbers after pressure from the Securities and Exchange Commission for increased transparency. This change reveals a previously undisclosed key metric for the e-commerce giant.

title: Sensors And Data Help Restaurant Chain Cava Know What Its Customers Want Most
summary: Fast-casual restaurant chain Cava uses sensors and data not only to improve kitchen operations and customer flow but also to develop a new personalized customer loyalty program. This program will track individual ordering preferences to offer tailored deals and coupons, aiming to strengthen brand loyalty and integrate with their grocery store product line. Cava's expansion aims to bridge its restaurant presence with grocery sales of its dips and spreads.

title: Kroger fights back at Amazon-owned Whole Foods and launches an apparel brand
summary: Kroger announced it will launch an apparel brand in Fall 2018 as part of its "Kroger Restock" initiative, aiming to compete with Amazon-owned Whole Foods and diversify beyond groceries. This strategic move, which includes $9 billion in capital investments over three years, seeks to drive more shoppers to its stores and address slimming grocery margins, despite Kroger shares falling around 38 percent this year. The apparel line will initially roll out in Fred Meyer and Kroger Marketplace stores and will focus on modern, playful, and simple styles for children, young men, juniors, men, and women, including activewear.

title: Netflix CEO Reed Hastings: Sleep Is Our Competition
summary: Netflix CEO Reed Hastings states that sleep is Netflix's biggest competitor, highlighting the company's focus on capturing more of people's leisure time. The article discusses the global rise of binge-watching and binge-racing, with Hastings emphasizing Netflix's strategy to dominate TV and movie categories by offering content that encourages extensive viewing, even overseas where linear TV is prevalent. He also clarifies that Netflix has no plans to venture into areas like video games or sports, preferring to add value within their core offerings and expand original content internationally.

title: Anthem CEO Joseph Swedish to step down, will be replaced by Gail Boudreaux
summary: Anthem announced that CEO Joseph Swedish will step down, to be replaced by Gail Boudreaux, former CEO of UnitedHealthcare. Swedish will serve as executive chairman until May 2018, then as a senior adviser. Boudreaux is expected to lead Anthem's new phase of growth, including the rollout of its integrated PBM, IngenioRx.

title: Target Enters Holiday Fray With Deals, Deals and More Deals
summary: Target is launching its Black Friday and broader holiday strategy with "lowest prices ever" and new offers, including automatic discounts and early access for Red cardholders. The retailer plans extensive deals throughout the season, including Cyber Monday and Weekend Deals, and has implemented a minimum wage increase and premium holiday pay for its employees to support the holiday shopping period. This strategy aims to regain customer perception of Target's competitive pricing.

title: Israeli talent ‘very important’ for Cadence business, CEO says
summary: Lip-Bu Tan, CEO of Cadence Design Systems, emphasized the critical role of Israeli talent and technology for the company's global business. Cadence, a developer of software for chipmakers, actively seeks Israeli acquisitions and employs around 250 people in its Israeli R&D center, citing the country's skilled workforce and vibrant semiconductor industry. Tan also highlighted the importance of a humble, innovative, and inclusive company culture for success, drawing parallels to teamwork in basketball.

title: CVS plans free same-day delivery in some cities, next-day delivery nationwide
summary: CVS Health Corp. is enhancing its prescription delivery services, starting with free same-day delivery in Manhattan in December and expanding next-day deliveries nationwide early next year. This move is aimed at leveraging its extensive store network and combating competition from online retailers like Amazon. The company also reported a significant drop in its third-quarter profit due to network exclusions and hurricane impacts, though its total revenue increased.

title: The Walt Disney Company Held & Ceased Talks to Purchase Parts of 21st Century Fox
summary: The Walt Disney Company engaged in and subsequently ended discussions to acquire the non-news and sports divisions of 21st Century Fox. This potential deal would have brought valuable assets like 20th Century Fox and the Fox Television Network under Disney's umbrella, opening possibilities for Marvel crossovers and exclusive content for Disney's upcoming streaming service. However, 21st Century Fox aimed to focus on its news and sports channels, and Disney avoided acquiring broadcast networks due to anti-trust concerns.

title: Ten trends redefining enterprise IT infrastructure
summary: The IT infrastructure landscape is experiencing rapid disruption, driven by ten key trends reshaping both provider and customer strategies. These trends include the shift to as-a-service models, mainstream adoption of public cloud, increased open-source usage, and evolving hardware and software architectures, presenting both opportunities and risks for industry players. The article highlights how familiar trends are accelerating and new developments are emerging, impacting cybersecurity, hardware sourcing, and the integration of AI and machine learning.

title: Ingram Micro Takes on ScanSource with Phoenix Group Buy
summary: Ingram Micro has acquired The Phoenix Group, a distributor of point-of-sale products and services, to expand its presence in rival ScanSource's territory. This move is significant as it brings Phoenix Group's expertise in electronic payments and value-added POS deployment services to Ingram Micro, aiming to offer "unmatched capabilities" in the channel. A key player in the deal is Jeff Yelton, Ingram Micro's VP and GM of advanced solutions, who previously led ScanSource's POS and Barcoding unit.

title: Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN) Getting Ready to Accept Cryptocurrencies
summary: Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN) has registered three new domain names related to cryptocurrencies, signaling its potential entry into the digital currency market. This move, along with the growing popularity and value of cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin, suggests Amazon may soon start accepting digital currencies for payments. The article also highlights increasing interest in cryptocurrencies from investment banks and hedge funds.

title: Microsoft Corporation is Deep in Artificial Intelligence Waters
summary: Microsoft Corporation is increasingly recognized as a major player in artificial intelligence, with its advanced AI chips making their way into devices like the HoloLens and plans for broader integration. The company is also leveraging its BrainWave platform for cloud-based AI acceleration and aims to make its AI technologies available to partners and Azure customers. The author contends that Microsoft's AI strategy is clearly defined and poised for significant revenue generation, making MSFT stock a strong investment in the AI industry.

title: Kroger is using Google and Microsoft clouds to avoid paying Amazon
summary: Kroger, the largest grocery store chain, is strategically splitting its cloud computing investments between Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud, deliberately avoiding Amazon Web Services (AWS) due to competitive concerns following Amazon's acquisition of Whole Foods. Chris Hjelm, Kroger's CIO, stated that it doesn't make competitive sense to help grow Amazon's business. This move mirrors actions by other large retailers like Walmart and Target, who are also seeking alternative cloud providers.

title: $3.5 billion Schuylkill Yards breaks ground on future park
summary: Drexel University and Brandywine Realty Trust have broken ground on the $3.5 billion Schuylkill Yards project in University City, starting with a 1.3-acre public park called Drexel Square. This park, designed by SHoP Architects and West 8, is envisioned as a central gathering place for the innovation hub. The larger 15- to 20-year master plan includes 6.9 million square feet of new construction and aims to transform 14 acres of land, potentially serving as a site for Amazon's second headquarters.

title: Amazon brings the curtains down on Junglee.com, finally
summary: Amazon has officially shut down Junglee.com, integrating its peer-to-peer shopping and selling experience into Amazon.in through the "Local Finds" platform. Junglee, originally a comparison-shopping site acquired by Amazon in 1998, had undergone multiple pivots but struggled to find its identity in the Indian e-commerce market after Amazon's direct entry. This move solidifies Amazon's P2P push in India and marks the end of Junglee as an independent entity.

title: Kroger avoids the Amazon machine, prefers Google and Microsoft clouds
summary: Kroger announced the expansion of its cloud computing portfolio on the Google Cloud Platform, adding to existing contracts with Microsoft Azure and Pivotal. The grocery giant is actively avoiding AWS due to competitive reasons, especially after Amazon's acquisition of Whole Foods. Kroger is also forming a "cloud enablement team" to manage these new cloud operations.

title: Billionaire Mark Cuban: I'm sticking with Amazon and Netflix as my top stock holdings
summary: Billionaire investor Mark Cuban announced that Amazon and Netflix remain his top stock holdings due to their consistent growth. He emphasized his long-term investment strategy and reluctance to frequently switch holdings. Amazon and Netflix have shown significant stock appreciation, with Amazon up over 48% and Netflix over 50% year-to-date.

title: Nvidia bounces after earnings, datacenter revenue beats
summary: Nvidia's stock bounced after its Q3 2018 earnings beat Wall Street expectations, with datacenter revenue exceeding analyst estimates. The company reported EPS of $1.33 and revenue of $2.64 billion, boosting its dividend and announcing a $1.25 billion return to shareholders. Shares were up significantly on the year, and the company issued strong fourth-quarter revenue guidance.

title: Black Friday deals: Amazon sells Echo, Fire TV, Kindle at Whole Foods
summary: Amazon is selling its electronic devices, including Echos, Fire TVs, and Kindles, at over 100 Whole Foods Market stores ahead of Black Friday. This move is part of Amazon's strategy to integrate its companies and expand its reach into customers' lives, particularly targeting the affluent and tech-progressive Whole Foods clientele. Special Black Friday deals on these devices will be available both online and in some Whole Foods locations.

title: First bank in Singapore to launch new cloud-based data centre test
summary: DBS Bank announced a partnership with Equinix to transform one of its Singapore data centers into a cloud-optimized center test, significantly reducing its size and operating costs by 75%. This initiative supports DBS's commitment to sustainability by improving energy efficiency and aligns with its strategy to adopt cloud technologies for enhanced agility, scalability, and digital transformation. DBS has been actively migrating to cloud-optimized technology, resulting in substantial efficiency gains and increased capacity, and aims to shift 50% of its compute workload to the public cloud by 2018.

title: What Would a Hasbro-Mattel Merger Mean for Christmas?
summary: Hasbro, Inc. (HAS) has reportedly made an offer to acquire Mattel, Inc. (MAT), leading to a surge in both companies' stock prices. This potential merger is seen as a strategic move to consolidate market power in an industry challenged by e-commerce and could create a stronger entity to compete with major players like Amazon. While the news is based on unnamed sources and is speculative, it presents a potential exit opportunity for Mattel investors facing declining sales and a suspended dividend.

title: Amazon to produce 'Lord of the Rings' television series
summary: Amazon.com Inc has acquired the global television rights to "The Lord of the Rings" and plans to produce a multi-season series exploring new storylines preceding J.R.R. Tolkien's "The Fellowship of the Ring." This move is seen as Amazon's biggest and most expensive effort yet to attract viewers to its Prime streaming and shopping club, aiming for a global hit similar to HBO's "Game of Thrones" to drive Prime sign-ups. The project is expected to have high production costs and represents a shift in Amazon's video programming strategy towards recognized, branded entertainment.

title: Broadridge opens 160,000 sq. ft. office at 2 Gateway in Newark
summary: Broadridge Financial Solutions has opened a new 160,000-square-foot office at 2 Gateway Center in downtown Newark, serving as a divisional headquarters for 1,100 employees. The relocation from Jersey City was supported by a 10-year, $23.4 million Grow New Jersey tax credit and is seen as a significant boost to Newark's revitalization as a fintech hub. Company executives and public officials, including Mayor Ras Baraka, celebrated the move, highlighting Newark's appeal for attracting and retaining top talent in the financial technology sector.

title: Daimler trademark lawsuit alleges that Amazon.com doesn't do enough to prevent infringement and counterfeits
summary: Daimler AG has filed a lawsuit against Amazon.com, Inc., alleging federal trademark infringement due to Amazon's complicity in selling counterfeit Mercedes-Benz parts, specifically wheel center caps. Daimler claims Amazon's platform facilitates the sale of numerous fake goods and that Amazon has not done enough to prevent infringement, despite its own anti-counterfeiting policy. The lawsuit highlights quality issues with counterfeit products that damage Daimler's brand reputation and states Amazon has refused to implement sufficient solutions to address the problem.

title: Walmart lifts profit outlook on strong third-quarter results
summary: Walmart raised its annual profit outlook after reporting strong third-quarter results that surpassed Wall Street expectations, driven by aggressive discounting, store improvements, and expanded online services. The retailer's strategic acquisitions, a significant increase in online item offerings, and partnerships like the one with Lord & Taylor are key to its growth and efforts to compete with Amazon. Walmart's e-commerce sales grew 50 percent, and the company projects full-year earnings per share between $4.38 and $4.46, up from its previous outlook.

title: Marriott creates smart guestroom lab
summary: Marriott International has developed an IoT Guestroom Lab, partnering with Samsung and Legrand, to create smart hotel rooms that allow guests to control various room features through voice commands and apps. This initiative aims to personalize guest experiences by leveraging mobile and voice-enabled technology, with elements of the new technology expected to be rolled out within the next five years. Other hotel chains like Best Western and Wynn Las Vegas are also implementing voice-activated technology, indicating a growing trend in the hospitality industry.

title: Despite Amazon, brick stores are not dead yet
summary: New exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have launched allowing investors to bet on the decline of brick-and-mortar retail and the rise of online sales, reflecting a trend amplified by Amazon's growth. Despite these new investment tools and warnings of a retail "apocalypse," U.S. government data and recent company performance suggest that traditional stores, especially those adopting a "click and mortar" strategy or focusing on niche markets, are not only surviving but thriving. Large retailers like Walmart and Home Depot are demonstrating strong sales and using their distribution networks to compete effectively.

title: 5 tips for shopping for beauty products
summary: The article provides five tips for shopping for beauty products, emphasizing budgeting, online price comparison, following bloggers for product information, trying products before buying, and signing up for loyalty programs. It notes the increasing options for affordable beauty products from retailers like Walmart, Target, Ulta Beauty Inc., and online sites, and highlights strategies for consumers to save money and make informed purchasing decisions.

title: Target Marketing Mix (4Ps) & Marketing Strategy
summary: This article analyzes Target Corporation's marketing mix (4Ps: Product, Price, Place, Promotion) and extends it to the 7Ps (People, Process, Physical Evidence). It details Target's product variety, aggressive pricing strategies, extensive distribution network, and promotional tactics, including their "Expect more, pay less" slogan. The article also provides an overview of Target's history and mission as a leading discount retailer.

title: Why Apple’s HomePod Is Three Years Behind Amazon’s Echo
summary: Apple's HomePod speaker project was significantly delayed and underwent multiple revisions after Apple engineers discovered Amazon's Echo in 2014. Despite initially dismissing the Echo's sound quality, Apple struggled internally to define the HomePod's place in its ecosystem while Amazon gained a substantial lead with its voice-activated assistant, Alexa. The article suggests that the HomePod's late arrival and limited functionality compared to the Echo are due to Apple's internal indecision and project cancellations.

title: New ProShares ETF makes money when retail stocks get hit
summary: ProShares has launched a new exchange-traded fund, the Decline of the Retail Store ETF (EMTY), designed to profit from the struggles of traditional brick-and-mortar retailers. The fund achieves this by taking short positions against an index of 56 retail stocks, many of which have seen significant declines in 2017. This offers investors a new way to capitalize on the ongoing disruption in the retail sector caused by changing consumer shopping trends and the rise of e-commerce.

title: Vanguard Russell 3000 Index Fund ETF Shares (VTHR) Holdings
summary: The article details the holdings and profile of the Vanguard Russell 3000 Index Fund ETF Shares (VTHR). It lists the top 10 holdings, primarily large technology companies like NVIDIA, Apple, and Microsoft, and breaks down the sector weightings with technology being the largest. The ETF aims to track the performance of the Russell 3000 Index, representing about 98% of the U.S. equity market.

title: Amazon Black Friday records push Jeff Bezos’s fortune past $100 billion
summary: Amazon CEO Jeff Bezos's net worth exceeded $100 billion following record-breaking Black Friday sales which saw Amazon.com Inc. shares reach new highs. An analyst estimates that Amazon is capturing a significant portion, 45% to 50%, of Black Friday's online sales. The company's stock has risen 58% this year, significantly outperforming the S&P 500 index.

title: Coca-Cola embraces a digital future as consumers move online
summary: Coca-Cola is adapting to the shift in consumer purchasing habits by investing heavily in a digital future, including e-commerce, meal kits, voice ordering, and direct-to-consumer shipments. This strategic move aims to maintain brand relevance as a significant portion of grocery sales move online. While direct-to-consumer is a growing business, the company's CEO believes the majority of sales will still go through customer platforms like Walmart and Amazon.

title: Shopify CEO Tobi Lutke joins ranks of Canadian billionaires as shares of tech company take off
summary: Tobi Lutke, CEO of Shopify Inc., has become a Canadian billionaire after the tech company's shares soared, recovering from a short-selling attack. His wealth reached US$1.1 billion from company shares, options, and sale proceeds. Shopify's shares have gained 588% since its 2015 trading debut, making it the second-best performing stock on Canada's S&P/TSX Composite Index this year.

title: AWS launches GuardDuty, its new intelligent threat detection service
summary: AWS has launched GuardDuty, a new intelligent threat detection service that uses machine learning to identify security threats and misconfigurations within AWS accounts. The service monitors various data streams, categorizes threats, and provides recommendations for mitigation, with options to integrate with third-party tools. This allows AWS users to proactively address security issues, leveraging the same tooling philosophy that AWS itself uses to manage its vast infrastructure with minimal human intervention.

title: This Week's ETF Launches: Betting on the Demise of Retail
summary: This article discusses new ETF launches, specifically focusing on two ProShares ETFs designed to profit from the decline of brick-and-mortar retail. The ProShares Long Online/Short Stores ETF (CLIX) and the ProShares Decline of the Retail Store ETF (EMTY) aim to capitalize on the shift from traditional in-store shopping to online retail. The article also touches on the Innovator IBD 50 ETF's transition from active to passive management.

title: Here’s what cities are offering Amazon to host its new headquarters
summary: Amazon's call for proposals for a second corporate headquarters (HQ2) sparked a national bidding war among 238 cities, with the tech giant planning to invest $5 billion and create up to 50,000 high-paying jobs. Cities are offering massive incentive packages and showcasing unique selling points like infrastructure and skilled labor pools to attract Amazon, which is seeking a metropolitan area with over 1 million people, strong universities, and a business-friendly environment. The decision on HQ2 could transform the chosen city, though experts caution about the tradeoffs and potential economic impact for different urban areas.
